concepts.name: Cells, rows, columns, ranges
concepts.summary: Identify cells by column-row address and describe ranges, rows, columns and worksheets in a workbook.

concepts.name: Entering and editing data
concepts.summary: Enter text, numbers and dates into cells and understand how the spreadsheet interprets and displays each type.

concepts.name: Basic number and text formatting
concepts.summary: Apply number, currency, percent, date and alignment formats and explain that formatting changes display rather than the stored value.

concepts.name: Simple formulas with operators
concepts.summary: Write formulas starting with an equals sign using +, -, *, / and cell references so results update when inputs change.

concepts.name: Core summary functions
concepts.summary: Use SUM, AVERAGE, MIN, MAX and COUNT on a range and explain what each returns.

concepts.name: Row and column layout adjustments
concepts.summary: Insert, delete, resize, hide and freeze rows and columns to make a sheet readable.

misconceptions.text: Typing a calculated result into a cell is the same as using a formula.
Formatting a cell as a percent or currency changes the underlying number.
A cell's displayed text is always exactly what is stored in it.

concepts.name: Relative and absolute references
concepts.summary: Copy formulas using relative, absolute and mixed references and predict how addresses change.

concepts.name: Sorting data
concepts.summary: Sort a data table by one or more columns while keeping rows intact.

concepts.name: Filtering data
concepts.summary: Filter a table by text, number or date criteria to show only matching rows without deleting others.

concepts.name: Conditional logic with IF
concepts.summary: Write IF formulas with comparison operators to return different results depending on a condition.

concepts.name: Conditional aggregation functions
concepts.summary: Use SUMIF, COUNTIF and AVERAGEIF to total or count only cells meeting a criterion.

concepts.name: Basic chart creation
concepts.summary: Create column, line and pie charts from a range and add titles, axis labels and legends.

concepts.name: Conditional formatting rules
concepts.summary: Apply rules that highlight cells by value, threshold or duplicate status.

misconceptions.text: Sorting a single column on its own is safe even when neighboring columns hold related data.
Filtering a table deletes the rows that are hidden.
Copying a formula always keeps pointing at the same cells it originally referenced.

concepts.name: Lookup functions
concepts.summary: Retrieve values from a table by key using lookup functions, choosing exact match and handling missing keys.

concepts.name: Nested and combined logic
concepts.summary: Combine IF with AND, OR and other functions to model multi-condition rules and analyse where they fail.

concepts.name: Text and date functions
concepts.summary: Clean, split and combine text and calculate with dates using text and date functions.

concepts.name: Structured data preparation
concepts.summary: Organize data as a flat table with one header row, consistent types and no blanks or merged cells, and diagnose issues that break analysis.

concepts.name: Pivot table construction
concepts.summary: Build pivot tables with row, column, value and filter fields to summarize a dataset by category.

concepts.name: Data validation controls
concepts.summary: Restrict cell entries with lists and rules to prevent invalid input.

concepts.name: Formula error diagnosis
concepts.summary: Interpret error values and use auditing tools to locate and fix formula problems.

concepts.name: Chart selection and design
concepts.summary: Choose chart types suited to the comparison being made and remove misleading or cluttered design.

misconceptions.text: Pivot tables update automatically the moment source data changes.
Merging cells and leaving blank rows makes data tables cleaner for analysis.
Approximate-match lookup is fine as a default on unsorted data.

concepts.name: Named ranges and structured tables
concepts.summary: Use tables and named ranges so formulas stay readable and expand automatically as data grows.

concepts.name: Dynamic array formulas
concepts.summary: Use array-returning functions that spill results and analyse when they outperform copied formulas.

concepts.name: Pivot calculations and slicers
concepts.summary: Extend pivot tables with grouping, calculated fields, percent-of measures and slicers for interactive analysis.

concepts.name: Model structure and assumptions
concepts.summary: Evaluate and design workbooks that separate inputs, calculations and outputs and document assumptions.

concepts.name: What-if and sensitivity analysis
concepts.summary: Use Goal Seek and scenario tools to test how changing inputs affects results and judge reliability.

concepts.name: Cross-sheet and external data
concepts.summary: Combine data from multiple sheets, files or imports and manage refresh and link risks.

concepts.name: Dashboard design
concepts.summary: Assess and assemble charts, pivots and key figures into a clear dashboard that answers specific questions.

misconceptions.text: A workbook that produces the right number today is a sound model.
Goal Seek proves the answer is realistic, not just mathematically achievable.
Linked external data is always current and safe from broken links.

concepts.name: Reusable formula patterns
concepts.summary: Design reusable calculations with LET, LAMBDA or named functions that reduce duplication and error.

concepts.name: Automation with macros and scripts
concepts.summary: Create macros or scripts to automate repetitive workbook tasks and judge when automation is warranted.

concepts.name: Workbook performance optimization
concepts.summary: Evaluate causes of slow workbooks, such as volatile functions and whole-column array calculations, and redesign for speed.

concepts.name: Spreadsheet risk and auditing
concepts.summary: Evaluate workbooks for hidden errors, hard-coded values and logic flaws using systematic review and checks.

concepts.name: Collaboration and access governance
concepts.summary: Judge and set protection, permissions and versioning practices for shared workbooks.

concepts.name: Choosing the right tool
concepts.summary: Decide when a spreadsheet is the right tool versus a database, BI tool or code, based on scale, integrity and repeatability.

concepts.name: Designing templates for others
concepts.summary: Build self-explanatory templates with validation, guidance and protection so non-experts can use them correctly.

misconceptions.text: Any spreadsheet problem is best solved by adding more formulas or macros.
Formulas that return no errors are correct.
Sheet protection or hiding is a secure way to guard sensitive data.
